title: Checkpoint: pips, lots, leverage and margin

questions.prompt: USD/JPY moves from 151.30 to 150.80. How many pips is that?

options.explanation: Right: the move is 0.50, and on a yen pair 0.50 ÷ 0.01 = 50 pips.
No: 5 pips on a yen pair would be 0.05.
No: that uses 0.0001 as the pip, which is wrong for yen pairs.

questions.prompt: EUR/USD, 0.30 lot with a 100,000-unit contract, account in USD. What is one pip worth?

options.explanation: No: that would be 3,000 units, which is 0.03 lot.

questions.prompt: EUR/USD at 1.2000, 0.10 lot (10,000 EUR), leverage 1:30, account in USD. What margin is required?

options.explanation: No: that forgets to convert 10,000 EUR into USD first.
No: that is the full trade value, before leverage.

questions.prompt: Balance 1,500 USD, open loss 300 USD, used margin 600 USD. What is the margin level?

options.explanation: No: that uses the balance. Margin level uses equity, which includes the open loss.
No: that divides margin by equity, which is the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains
options.explanation: True: profit and loss come from the full trade size.

options.text: Swaps can be positive or negative and vary by broker
options.explanation: True: check your broker's contract specification.

options.text: Stop-out levels are the same at every broker
options.explanation: False: each broker sets its own margin call and stop-out levels.
